summary: An independent review of the new start screen and guides (a code reviewer, a hands-on tester, a first-time user of 60 and a designer, then two skeptics who tried to disprove each finding) confirmed 24 problems, and all are fixed. The biggest: a guide left alone for a month could never be picked up again, typing on some step pages could be lost without a warning, and the retirement and protect-your-family guides could say "finished" while their answer pages still asked for more.
points: A guide you have not touched for 30 days comes back as soon as you tap Continue or a step.
Before you move on, any typing on the page that is not saved yet gets a warning, whether or not the page uses a form; a second tap goes on.
The retirement guide now needs your spending before "See if the money lasts", and the protect guide gathers savings and bills before the life insurance check.
Skip goes to a step you can do now, says what it skipped at the top of the next page, and a step that needs an earlier one shows "Do step 2 first" instead.
After a page sends you elsewhere (bringing in a bank file opens the sorting page), the next page offers "‹ Back to the guide".
Clearer words: each "does not apply" says what you said, Quick answers' rows read as plain questions.
numbers: 39 findings; 24 confirmed by the skeptics and fixed, 15 rejected as taste or already decided

shots.caption: After "Skip to": the skip is confirmed at the top, and this look-only step says plainly what counts as done.
"See what lenders see" needs your pay first, so the guide sends you to step 2 instead of letting it count.
